summary: Defines the publication stream for RFCs coming from the Internet Research Task Force. Most documents will come from IRTF research groups and are expected to be published as Informational or Experimental. It is informational.

eli5.summary: The IRTF is a group for long-term research. This document sets up the special path its writings take to be published as RFCs.

subtitle: The process that lets Internet Research Task Force documents become RFCs with an IRTF label.

tldr.problem: Research groups in the Internet Research Task Force wanted a clear, reviewed path to publish their findings in the RFC series under an IRTF label.
tldr.mechanism: A research group reviews its own document, the Internet Research Steering Group (IRSG) reviews and approves it, the IESG checks for conflicts with standards work, and then the RFC Editor publishes it.
tldr.outcome: IRTF stream documents are expected to come out as Informational or Experimental RFCs and are never candidates for any level of Internet Standard.

facts.label: Standards track
facts.value: Never a candidate for any level of Internet Standard

today: RFC 5743 is an Informational document, and the unit metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated. It defines the IRTF stream process as it stood in December 2009.

sections.title: The IRTF Document Stream
sections.content:
The Internet Research Task Force (IRTF) sometimes wants to publish a document in the RFC series. This memo defines the steps for doing so through the IRTF stream. Document streams are described in RFC 4844. Most documents are expected to come from IRTF Research Groups and to be published as Informational or Experimental RFCs by the RFC Editor.

The stream lets research groups publish findings with an IRTF label. Pre-publication editorial review by the IRSG improves readability and makes sure proper caveats are applied. The memo says it was updated after over a year of experience with roughly a dozen documents, and that the IRTF concluded the benefits and process are sound.
sections.eli5: Scientists in the IRTF want to share their ideas as official RFCs. This document says how their writing gets checked before it is published.

sections.title: What a Research Group Must Do First
sections.content:
Before anything else, the Research Group (RG) must review the document for editorial and technical quality. The memo lists guidelines for the document itself. The abstract must say it is a product of the RG, and a paragraph near the beginning must describe the level of support for publication, for example consensus or controversy. The breadth of review the document has received must be noted.

It must also be very clear throughout that the document is not an IETF product and is not a standard. If it describes an experimental protocol, appropriate usage caveats must be present, and if the protocol was considered in an IETF working group before, the introduction must say so. There should be citations to relevant research publications. The RG also names a document shepherd who tracks and helps the document along to publication.
sections.eli5: Before turning in homework, the research group checks it, says who agrees with it, and writes clearly that it is a research idea and not an official rule.

sections.title: IRSG, IESG and RFC Editor Steps
sections.content:
The IRSG acts like an editorial review board and approves all IRTF-stream documents intended for RFC publication. Its review is not a deep technical review, which belongs in the RG. At least one IRSG member who is not a chair of that research group must review the document and the RG's editorial process. Reviewers look for clear writing, a critical reading from non-experts, adequate review within the RG, and proper citations. Reviews are written to be public. All IRSG comments must be addressed, though the RG need not accept every one. If the IRSG does not approve, the document returns to the RG with feedback, and in rare cases it may be judged unsuitable for the stream.

Next, the IRTF Chair gives the IESG a chance to review it under RFC 5742. The scope is only to ensure that the Informational and Experimental designations are not misused to circumvent the Internet Standards Process. The IESG is expected to respond, normally within four weeks.

Finally, the IRTF Chair asks the RFC Editor to publish. The document enters the queue at the same priority as non-standard IETF-stream and IAB-stream documents, and the shepherd helps during AUTH48 review. The RFC Editor inserts the Status of this Memo labels and text identifying it as an IRTF product, as defined in RFC 5741.
sections.eli5: First the group checks its work, then a review board checks it again, then another board makes sure it is not pretending to be a rule, and finally the editor prints it.

sections.title: Rights, Patents and Trademarks
sections.content:
The IRTF stream aims for research to have broad impact, so publication rights should in general not restrict republication with proper citation. Authors submit their material as Internet-Drafts and grant rights as described in RFC 5378. The IETF Trust grants readers the right to make unlimited derivative works unless the RFC says no derivative works are permitted. Authors may request no derivative works, but the IRTF Chair may question whether that is appropriate. The final publication decision rests with the IRTF Chair, and following the terms does not guarantee publication.

Contributors follow the IETF IPR rules, including disclosure of known patent and trademark issues, using the IETF's IPR disclosure mechanism. The IRTF prefers liberal terms with no fees or licensing and non-discriminatory terms, but there are no specific requirements on licensing terms.
sections.eli5: Authors agree that other people may copy and build on their work as long as they give credit, and they must tell everyone about any patents they know of.

sections.title: IAB Statement and Security
sections.content:
As the body that approves the creation of document streams, the Internet Architecture Board (IAB) reviewed this proposal and supports it as an operational change in line with the respective roles of the IRTF, IESG and RFC Editor.

The memo states that there are no security considerations in the document. Appendix A lists the IRSG membership at the time of writing, along with the research groups members represented.
sections.eli5: The group in charge of the rules for RFC paths said this plan is fine, and there is nothing in it that affects computer security.
